scenes.narration: In a green meadow at the edge of the woods, there lived a hare. He was quick, he was clever, and he was very, very proud.
Every morning he raced the wind across the grass. "Nobody in the whole wide world," he boasted, "is as fast as me!"
One day, the hare met a tortoise plodding slowly along the path. "Ha!" he laughed. "You are so slow, you will never get anywhere at all!"
The tortoise blinked her old, wise eyes. "Slow I may be," she said, "but I will race you, if you like."
News of the race spread through the woods. All the animals came to watch, and the fox waved the flag: ready, steady, go!
Whoosh! Off shot the hare, so fast that the flowers bent over in the wind. And off went the tortoise too: step, step, step.
Soon the hare was far, far ahead. He looked back, and he could not even see the tortoise. "I have plenty of time," he yawned. "I think I'll take a little nap."
The sun climbed high into the sky. The hare snored, and dreamed of winning. But the tortoise kept on walking: step, step, step.
Past the pond, up the hill, and right past the sleeping hare she went. Step, step, step.
When at last the hare woke up, the sun was going down. He leapt to his feet and ran as fast as he could!
But it was too late. The tortoise was already crossing the finish line, and all the animals cheered and cheered.
The hare hung his head. And the tortoise smiled a slow, kind smile. "Slow and steady," she said, "wins the race."
